_comment: What a package still cannot bring in its own folder, and what a package written at runtime (the LLM package builder, roadmap item 20) still cannot rely on (src/portability.py serves this to Dev Lab ▸ Builder readiness). Each anchor is `path::text` and must still be in that file while the gap is open; test_portability.py fails when one is gone, so closing a gap means changing its status here in the same change. kind: runtime | gate | tooling | commons | code | client | watch | docs | devlab. impact on a dropped-in or built package: blocks (it fails a gate, cannot be written or cannot be served), degrades (it works, worse or silently wrong), cosmetic. status: open | done (with `closed`, the day, and `evidence`, `path::text` of the test that holds it — checked like an anchor) | by_design (the engine's vocabulary is the contract between packages and the engine). roadmap: the step of docs/roadmap.md (9.x, 20.x) that closes it. steps: the roadmap steps of the builder's foundation, in order, each titled as docs/roadmap.md titles it; a step is done when it says so (`done`, the day) or when every gap citing it is.
verdict: The code is package-neutral, and since item 20 a package written while the app runs is stored, checked by one gate, read privately beside the shipped ones for its owner, may bring its own vocabulary, and has one spec. What is open below is the builder itself (docs/roadmap.md item 21): the job a build runs as, the model loop, the screens on the web and the phone, and the production steps.

steps.title: One package spec; a package from nothing
The trace says what each engine decided
The build as a durable job
Web: the builder in the program builder

gaps.title: A build has nowhere to run
gaps.detail: A build takes minutes; a request has 120 s and one of four threads. The only job the server keeps is an in-memory dictionary lost on every deploy, and the durable queue it has (Garmin's) never re-claims a row left processing and is not started at boot.

gaps.title: Nothing calls a model
gaps.detail: No LLM SDK, no key, no prompt: the spec and the gate exist, the loop that writes files, checks them and fixes what the gate finds does not.

gaps.title: The web's builder zeroes a package's own modalities
gaps.detail: The program builder sends priority overrides built from the modality list compiled into the build, and the server replaces the goal's priorities with them: a method made of its own modalities is sent all zeros and generates nothing.

gaps.title: No way to describe a method on the web
gaps.detail: The program builder lists philosophies; it has no card to create one, no progress for a build, and no list of the athlete's own.

gaps.title: The phone fetches the philosophies once
gaps.detail: A method built while the app is open never appears: the list is loaded when empty and never again.

gaps.title: No way to describe a method on the phone
gaps.detail: The phone's builder has no card to create a method, no progress for a build, and no list of the athlete's own.

gaps.title: Nothing shows what a build did
gaps.detail: A build's turns, checks, the problems the gate found and the tokens it spent are the only way to judge quality and cost; no screen reads them.

gaps.title: Production has no table, key or role for it
gaps.detail: Migrations 013 (and 014, with the build job) are not run on production, the model's key is not a Fly secret, and no account carries the dev role for it. Until then the builder says it is unavailable. Each is a step for the owner, after scripts/backup_prod.sh.

gaps.title: The gates cannot be called for one package
gaps.detail: Was: check_styles and check_provenance looped every philosophy and printed, and add_package shelled out. Now src/package_gate.check_package(folder) runs the gates' own code for one folder, stage by stage — files, schema, ids, a smoke generate of every track and phase, provenance — and returns structured problems; the tools and the MCP server call the same code. It needs the folder in the loader's packages directory until 20.3.

gaps.title: One packages folder, and three paths that ignore it
gaps.detail: Was: TRAINING_PACKAGES_DIR replaced data/packages and never added to it. Now the loader reads two roots: the shipped packages, and for the caller in context an overlay of its own (loader.overlay, a context variable — no loader call takes a parameter). Every module reaches a package through loader.package_dirs / package_dir / package_files; validate_entities reads the loader's root. tools/run_checks.py still looks for package tests in the checkout it checks, which is what it is for.

gaps.title: One malformed package breaks loading for every package
gaps.detail: Was: one YAML error or missing id raised for every caller. The shipped root stays fail-fast, so the image build fails on a broken shipped package. An overlay package is probed once for exactly what the loaders index unguarded (every file parses, the philosophy is the folder's, each framework, archetype and exercise has an id) and one that fails is set aside whole (loader.quarantined) — nobody else's packages, and none of its owner's others, are touched.

gaps.title: An id two packages declare is resolved silently at load
gaps.detail: Among the shipped packages a collision is still refused by validate_entities --all and add_package. For a package written at runtime: the overlay only adds — a folder named as a shipped package is set aside, and a framework, archetype, philosophy or media id the shipped packages declare keeps the shipped copy — and the gate refuses the collision before install and, for an athlete's own package, any id without its owner's prefix (package_gate.check_package(owner_prefix=)).

gaps.title: Caches that outlive a package change
gaps.detail: Was: seven caches filled once per process and never cleared. Now whatever a module keeps from the packages is kept per view (loader.view_store, loader.scoped_cache: the shipped view for the life of the process, the few most recent overlays beside it) — standards, exercise media, similarity, the analytics digest, test archetypes, derived lifts, session icons, watch owners, Explore's documents and links, the bells — and api.invalidate_package_data() forgets all of it in one call.

gaps.title: The reference routes are one answer for everyone
gaps.detail: Was: one answer per path for everyone, and clearing it abandoned the image's baked build for the life of the process. The shared answers and the build are untouched. An athlete with packages of their own (the reference routes read the bearer token when there is one, never requiring it) gets a variant built in their view, kept in a bounded store keyed by their overlay directory — named from their packages' revisions, so an install or a removal is a new key and nothing is cleared — and sent `Cache-Control: private` with `Vary: Authorization`. A route their packages do not change keeps the shared bytes.

gaps.title: Nowhere to keep a package written at runtime
gaps.detail: Was: packages lived only in the image, whose disk is lost on every deploy. Now an athlete's own package is a row in user_packages (migration 013): a capped file map of YAML text. src/package_store.py lays the athlete's set out as folders for the loader — a directory named from every (package, revision), built beside the old one and renamed in, so any process or machine builds the same one and no reader sees half of it. Migration 013 has not been run on production; the store creates the table lazily (row security on, deny-by-default) until it is.
evidence: migrations/013_user_packages.sql::CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_packages

gaps.title: Every package is everyone's
gaps.detail: Was: any folder with a philosophy.yaml was everyone's. An athlete's package is read only inside their own view: require_auth names their overlay for the length of the request (auth._as_user; asked only if a loader runs, always reset), every store read takes the user id, the table's row security is per user, and each id the package declares carries its owner's prefix. The reference routes that take no sign-in still answer the shipped packages alone (20.4).

gaps.title: The API can author entities, never a package
gaps.detail: The entity routes still write only `custom` (a shipped-root, developer path). A whole package now has its own way in: POST /api/packages takes a file map, runs every gate with the owner's prefix (dry_run checks only), stores it when it passes and answers the gate's problems when it does not; GET lists and reads back, DELETE removes (409 while the athlete's program is built from it). Behind the authoring gate until the builder ships.

gaps.title: A new modality is a commons edit
gaps.detail: Was: modalities loaded from data/commons only, while the schemas told an author to define one in the package. A package now declares its own in vocabulary.yaml — a modality (recovery cost, session position, progression model, display) with the analytics family it rolls up into — read for the package and whoever borrows from it, never replacing a commons id. The scheduler, the families and GET /api/modalities read it; the web draws a modality it has never met from the served display (the phone falls back to a neutral style: client_vocab_compiled). The schema texts now say where a new one is declared.

gaps.title: A new movement pattern is a commons edit
gaps.detail: Was: a pattern outside the commons' recovery table failed a gate, and nothing said so to an author. A package's vocabulary.yaml declares its patterns with the body regions each loads; regional recovery reads them beside the commons'. A pattern nobody declares is now a finding of the id check (portability, the gate's `unknown_id`), which says to declare it. Slot-filter aliases stay the commons': a slot names a package pattern directly.

gaps.title: Injury flags protect only the exercises the commons name
gaps.detail: A package pattern must say which injury flags rule it out (`excluded_by`, required — [] is an answer), and it joins those flags' excluded patterns, so an exercise that names only package patterns is still filtered for an injured athlete. The commons' flags still list shipped exercise ids for what a pattern does not catch; a package states the same per exercise with `contraindicated_with`.

gaps.title: New equipment is a commons edit
gaps.detail: Was: an implement outside the commons' list failed four schema enums and no athlete could tick it. A package's vocabulary.yaml lists its own (`equipment`: id and label). The validator widens the schemas' equipment enums — still generated from the commons — by what the file's package and the packages it borrows from add; the equipment list (src/equipment.items, GET /api/equipment) carries them after the commons' with their `package`; the web's pickers and Profile file them under "From your packages". An athlete without one gets none of its exercises, as for any implement.

gaps.title: The phone's vocabulary is compiled in
gaps.detail: The web now draws a package's modality from the served display and lists a package's implements in its pickers (20.6, 20.7). The phone and the watches still read only the tables generated into them at build time: a package modality draws in the neutral style with its id for a name, and the phone's equipment picker cannot offer a package implement — an athlete who builds on the phone cannot tick it, so the exercises that need it are filtered out. Closing it means the Apple targets reading GET /api/modalities and /api/equipment, and a release.

gaps.title: No one document says how to write a package
gaps.detail: Was: the outline was spread over four documents, none of which shipped, and the MCP templates carried stale lists. docs/schemas/PACKAGE_SPEC.md is the one document — what a package is, each file, how a week is built, every valid value, the gate, an athlete's own package, common mistakes, a worked example — in the part of docs/ the image carries. Its lists and its example are generated (tools/gen_package_spec.py --check, a push gate). The server serves it (GET /api/dev/package-spec, with the asker's id prefix and the limits) and so does the MCP server (get_package_spec); the MCP skeleton prints its value lists from the schemas when asked and passes every gate.

gaps.title: The drop-in test runs renamed copies of audited packages
gaps.detail: test_packages/scratch_minimal is a package written from nothing — its own exercise ids, modality, movement pattern and implement. test_package_dropin.py drops it in beside the three copies and runs it through the same end-to-end checks; test_private_packages.py installs it for one athlete while the process runs, under that athlete's prefix, and another athlete sees none of it; test_package_overlay.py and test_private_packages.py cover the malformed package (set aside alone) and the one that fails the gate (not stored).

gaps.title: The generation trace covers the scheduler, not the engines that run
gaps.detail: Was: a contract traced its id and module ids, a template week its categories, a test nothing. Each week now says its `engine`. A contract's week carries `contract_week`: the modules with their minutes, period week, step, model and deload, the placement chosen and the next best with their scores, optional work left short and the test; each session its `module_steps`. A template's week carries `template`: the days kept and dropped and, for each day, every pool asked, where its rotation stood, what was passed over and why, what was taken. A test session is marked with what it measures and stands in for; a week lists its placed and skipped tests. A composition carries each track's own decisions (`lane_weeks`) and its kept days. The trace is asked for, never paid for: the program is the same with it. Left: a passed-over workout says it does not fit as written, not which of level, equipment, injury or minutes ruled it out.

gaps.title: Pipeline Trace draws the scheduler's steps
gaps.detail: Was: allocation and day assignment, empty for every shipped package; no way to ask for a composition; nothing of what the program says about itself. The Schedule step's card and the flow now follow the engine that built the week (EngineWeek.tsx): a contract's modules, steps and placement against the next best; a template's days, pools, rotation and what was passed over; a composition's tracks, each on its own. The form takes a second track and its equipment list is the vocabulary's; a session says its test, its modules' steps, its track and what it stands in for; the Output step lists compromises, coverage and what the constraints held back. A trace can be linked to (`/dev?philosophy=…&run=1`). Left: a contract track's options are not asked in the form (the defaults run).
evidence: frontend/src/components/devlab/DevLabPanels.test.tsx::the flow follows the engine that built the week

gaps.title: Model Interactions' map is written in the component
gaps.detail: Was: the strip and its five edges were constants in the component, describing the scheduler's path as the pipeline, with nothing held to the code. The map is data (tools/model_map.json): eleven interactions — the track and its phases, a contract's week, a template's week, the scheduler's allocation and archetype score, slots and exercises, loads, compositions, tests, the athlete's constraints, which packages a caller sees — each with what it reads, what the engine decides, the constants in code and the anchors test_model_map.py checks. The server adds which engine each track runs on (twelve on contracts, ten on templates, none on the scheduler), and the panel reads the map one engine at a time, starting with the busiest or the last program's.
evidence: frontend/src/components/devlab/DevLabPanels.test.tsx::reads the map one engine at a time

gaps.title: No Impact tab
gaps.detail: Dev Lab ▸ Impact sends the Pipeline Trace form's request to POST /dev/constraint-impact and lays the answer out: how many sessions change and how many directly, per constraint what lifting it means and how many sessions and slots it accounts for, the equipment that would restore the most, every change with its causes and reasons (filtered by cause, knock-on changes on request), and for a refused request what alone would let it generate.

gaps.title: Progression models, contract models and slot types are engine vocabulary
gaps.detail: A package chooses among them; a new one is engine work: how a load progresses (linear, RPE, time to task, density, as written…), how a contract module schedules (a density cycle, a ladder…) and what a slot type means to the dispatcher. The rest of the vocabulary is data since 2026-10-31: phase kinds (phase_kinds.yaml), training levels (training_levels.yaml) and intensities (intensities.yaml), each read through one module and generated into the clients and the schemas.

gaps.title: Recovery ranking, the high-cost floor and the load defaults are engine semantics
gaps.detail: What a recovery cost means (its rank, and the 48 h between two high-cost modalities, which a framework can waive per pair: recovery.allow_consecutive) and the defaults a slot falls back to when its package says nothing (2.5 kg a week, 3 × 5, two sessions a week). The numbers that vary are data since 2026-10-31: the RPE load factors and the weekly ramps (progression.yaml; a framework's progression_defaults overrides the ramps), each level's distance share (training_levels.yaml) and each intensity's recovery weight (intensities.yaml).
